documents.title: Part B Technical Description (CEF Transport Standard)

sub.label: Project description, scope and objectives
prompts: Overall objective
General description and context (including political priorities and if part of a global project)
Location on network/corridors
Justification (current situation and needs analysis)
Specific objectives linked to work packages
Expected outcomes and results (quantitative information: km, MVA, Bcm/y, kV, bar, etc.)

sub.label: Global projects
prompts: Objectives of the global project
General description and context (specify how project fits into global project)
Justification (problems, needs and issues)
State of play, results and objectives achieved so far
Parallel projects and links to project
Timetable and interdependencies

sub.label: 1.1 TEN-T network - Project of common interest (PCI)
prompts: Why project is considered PCI within Article 7 of TEN-T Regulation
How it contributes or links to core and/or comprehensive network
Does it contribute to corridor work plans and implementing acts per Article 47
Does it produce network effect by linking with or complementing other TEN-T/CEF actions

sub.label: 1.2 Call objectives and priorities
prompts: How project contributes to objectives, priorities and expected results of the topic

sub.label: 1.3 EU added value
prompts: Effects of project from EU interest perspective
How it contributes to European-level objectives

sub.label: 1.4 Cross-border link
prompts: Is project related to cross-border links in Part III of CEF Regulation Annex
Continuity of PCI or core network corridor (YES/NO)
High degree of integration in planning and implementation (YES/NO)
Other joint commitments by Member States/neighbouring countries (YES/NO)

sub.label: 1.5 Integrated management
prompts: Is project a cross-border link with integrated management structure including joint ventures (YES/NO)
Main elements of integration agreement

sub.label: 1.6 Synergies
prompts: Synergies with other CEF sectors (Energy and Digital)
Synergies with other EU programmes (RRF, Digital Europe, Horizon Europe, Structural Funds, etc.)
Does project include synergetic elements eligible under another CEF sector
Will project benefit from funding from another programme

sub.label: 1.7 Dual-use potential (civilian-defence)
prompts: Potential of dual-use (civilian-defence) for Military mobility topics

sub.label: 2.1 Readiness and technical maturity
prompts: Readiness and technical maturity of project
State of preparation for every work package (terms of reference, tendered, contract signed, started, etc.)
How implementation depends on results of past or ongoing feasibility/technical studies
For high-technology projects (infrastructure, ITS, cooperative ITS, airspace): technology type, communication, materials
Critical dependencies: connection to grid/utilities, access to land, authorisations status

sub.label: 2.1a Ex ante evaluations and feasibility studies
prompts: Information on ex-ante evaluations and feasibility studies and main results
Objectives, activities and policy options considered
Main indicators used in ex-ante evaluation
Strategic and technical alternative options in option analysis
Multi-criteria analysis or other shortlisting method
Arguments for excluding cheaper but still relevant solutions

sub.label: 2.1b Political commitment
prompts: Information on political commitments regarding implementation
Cross-border commitments where relevant
Formal and informal documents demonstrating commitments (decisions, MoU, agreements, national strategies)

sub.label: 2.1c Public consultations
prompts: Public consultations carried out and feedback received
Consultations foreseen and their timing
Plans to involve stakeholders during implementation

sub.label: 2.2 Status of contracting procedures and authorisations, approvals and permits
prompts: General project maturity in terms of authorisations, approvals and permits needed

sub.label: 2.2a Authorisations, approvals and permits (including environmental)
prompts: For each work package/task: authorisations needed (governmental, regional, local, environmental, right-of-way, state aid)
Status and expected timeline
Risk factors and mitigating measures (alternative solutions) if not obtained in time

sub.label: 2.2b Building permits
prompts: For each work package/task: building permits description, authority, size (land surface), kind of works
Status and timeline
Risk factors and mitigating measures if not obtained in time

sub.label: 2.2c Contracting procedures
prompts: Procurement maturity in general
Contracts awarded before proposal submission: typology, status, procurement method (EU-wide/national, open/restricted/negotiated)
Contracts planned during implementation: typologies, procurement method selection, best value for money approach
Starting dates of awarded contracts

sub.label: 2.3 Financial maturity
prompts: Availability of funds for project over its lifecycle
Budget in balance; use of funds vs sources of funds
Distinction between own resources, third party resources, grants and other funding
Fund providers, recipients and use of funds for each source
Financing structure diagram
Revenues and other financing sources to complement CEF support
Degree of confidence in financial commitments
Own resources: internal approval status, conditions to reach approval, degree of confidence
Planning/timing for final investment decision
Third party resources: amounts expected, nature (equity, debt, other grants), expected approval timing
Due-diligence process scope if applicable
Debt structure (layers and seniority) if applicable
Alternatives if specific financing source not available

sub.label: 3.1 Cost effectiveness and financial management
prompts: For each work package: explanation and justification of resource levels needed
Human resources, financial resources, equipment purchases, etc.
Appropriateness of estimated costs (type and level)

sub.label: 3.1a Financial management
prompts: Detailed arrangements for financial management of project
Monitoring, internal and external audit and evaluation processes
Processes to ensure eligibility of expenditure

sub.label: 3.2 Consortium set-up, governance and organisational structure
prompts: Organisational structure to implement project
Distribution of roles and responsibilities between partners (Beneficiaries, Affiliated Entities, Associated Partners)
Main contractual arrangements, governance structure, lines of communication, decision-making processes
Status of governance body establishment, member nomination, governance rules approval
Pending decisions on organisational structure
Special purpose company/vehicle (SPC/SPV) shareholder agreement status

sub.label: 3.3 Project management, quality assurance and control procedures
prompts: Methods to ensure good quality, monitoring, planning and control
Main features of quality assurance plan
Quality control system to be used

sub.label: 3.4 Risk management
prompts: How risk management is part of project management approach
Risk management methods and procedures in general
Risk management plan status and main features

sub.label: 3.4a Risk assessment grid
prompts: Critical risks, uncertainties or difficulties related to implementation
Measures/strategy for addressing them
Significant risks, factors of uncertainty, major complexity elements
Political, institutional, financial, organisational, social and/or technical risks
Impact and likelihood (high, medium, low) for each risk
Proposed risk mitigation measures

sub.label: 3.5 Communication and visibility
prompts: Communication plan and strategy for EU funding visibility
Billboards, reports, websites, brochures, leaflets, newsletters, press articles, presentations
Websites and Social Media accounts being used
Communications contact person
Note: Separate project websites are not eligible; costs must be on participants' websites

sub.label: 3.6 Sustainability and maintenance strategy
prompts: Follow-up of project after EU funding ends
How proper maintenance and continued operation will be guaranteed
Detailed strategy (periodicity, components, financing, actors) and practical measures

sub.label: 4.1 Demand analysis
prompts: Results of demand/traffic forecast study (if any)
Overall context (date of completion) and scope of study
Methodology chosen
Assumptions regarding demand growth rate and utilisation rate on completion
List of indicators and sources of verification
If study goes beyond project scope: overview of global project demand analysis
Whether TEN-T/CEF or other EU programmes provided financial support

sub.label: 4.2 Economic and financial analysis
prompts: General socio-economic impact of project
Potential to generate cash revenues
Limitations (legal, regulatory, commercial) constraining revenue generation
Expected revenues and timeline (number and diversity of users)
User price sensitivity and captive user status
Degree of certainty of assumptions and estimations
Autonomous operation or dependence on additional investments
For full CBA works proposals: main results of economic analysis (ERR and ENPV)
CBA scope vs project scope differences
Use of unitary values from Handbook on External Costs of Transport

sub.label: 4.2a Financial analysis
prompts: Financial viability/sustainability of project over its lifecycle
Budget in balance; use of funds vs sources of funds
For CBA works proposals: Financial indicators after CEF funding (FRR and FNPV)
Comparison with national and international sector benchmarks
For negative FNPV projects: explanation of why proceeding despite insufficient financial viability
Demonstration of financial sustainability (positive cumulative cash flows)
Other sources of support (grants, subsidies) or revenue compensation
Financial risks associated with implementation

sub.label: 4.3 Social, environmental and other impacts
prompts: Expected impacts on congestion, modal split, safety and security, service quality, noise and air pollutants
Expected positive/negative impacts on time savings, capacity optimisation, service quality
Monetary value of impacts (EUR NPV) if quantified in CBA
Main assumptions (quantities and unit values)
Expected impacts on modal split
Expected impacts on safety and security (accidents, injuries, fatalities if quantified)
Expected impacts on noise emissions (quantified if in CBA)
Expected impacts on climate change targets (Paris Agreement, 2030 Climate and energy framework)
Expected impacts on air pollutants (PM2.5, NOX, SO2, etc.)

sub.label: 4.3a Environmental and climate impact
prompts: Positive/negative impacts on greenhouse gas emissions and global warming
Upstream and downstream emissions impact (full life cycle)
For works CBA proposals: monetary value of GHG impacts (EUR NPV) and unit values (EUR/tCO2 equivalent)
Climate change considerations in project design and components
Consistency with climate proofing infrastructure mitigation pillar
Cost of greenhouse gas emissions integration in economic evaluation
Consistency with energy efficiency first principle
Consistency with 2050 emission targets
Measures foreseen to monitor, prevent and mitigate negative environmental impact
Estimation of associated costs

sub.label: 4.3b Climate resilience (for Works topics)
prompts: Climate proofing exercise undertaken per Commission Technical guidance
Vulnerability assessment findings identifying climate hazards
Significant risks identified and mitigation approach
Vulnerabilities embedded in decision-making process
Relevant measures taken for project resilience to climate change

sub.label: 4.3c Decision-making tool, input for policy making or development of best practices (for Studies topics)
prompts: How project will have impact as decision-making tool or policy input
Development of best practices
Who will use project output and for how long
Extent to which output will be relied on for decision-making
Relation to other studies and future projects
Level of impact (CEF Transport action, national project, global project, etc.)
Relevance and economic value of future projects in costs and benefits
Extent to which project elements could develop best practices

sub.label: 4.3d Interoperability and accessibility
prompts: How project contributes to increased interoperability of transport systems and/or modes in TEN-T network
How proposal enhances accessibility for passengers and/or goods to TEN-T network
Cross-border dimension impact
Effect/contribution to territorial accessibility (including outermost regions and islands)

sub.label: 4.3e Innovation and digitalisation
prompts: How innovative technologies are being used to reach project objectives
How digitalisation forms part of project or its use
Reference of EU-supported research projects if applicable

sub.label: 4.3f Competition
prompts: Expected positive and/or negative impacts of project on regional and national competition

sub.label: 4.3g Regional and local development and land use
prompts: Expected positive and/or negative impacts on regional and/or local development
Land use impacts and assessment of neighbouring regions
Link to urban development plans
Contribution to land value increase

sub.label: 4.3h Outermost regions (if applicable)
prompts: Which outermost regions are impacted by the project
How regions and project promoters cooperate
Which countries are impacted
How cooperation with them is ensured

sub.label: 4.3i Other considerations
prompts: Any other relevant considerations

sub.label: 5.1 Financial gap
prompts: How EU grant will facilitate or accelerate project
Comparison to situation without EU funding
Financial gap description and justification
Amount specification and justification
Financial obstacles and how public funding helps overcome them
Expected EU support under Recovery and Resilience Facility (RRF) (approximate amount)

sub.label: 5.2 Public and private investment and financial leverage
prompts: Capacity of grant to trigger bigger investment
Allow other investments
Will EU grant help mobilising additional public and private funding
Different sources of funding or higher amounts availability
Financial leverage optimisation in terms of amounts and duration

sub.label: 5.3 Stakeholder commitment
prompts: How EU funding would reinforce commitment of different partners and stakeholders (public and private)
Effects on stakeholder commitment if project would not receive grant

sections.label: 6. WORK PLAN, WORK PACKAGES, ACTIVITIES, RESOURCES AND TIMING

sub.label: 6.1 Work plan
prompts: Brief description of overall work plan structure
List of work packages or graphical presentation (Pert chart or similar)

sub.label: 6.2 Work packages, activities, resources and timing
prompts: Detailed description of project activities grouped into work packages
Objective for each work package (expected outcome)
Activities, milestones and deliverables for each work package
Logical grouping guided by identifiable outputs
Minimum 2 work packages (WP1 for management/coordination/cross-cutting)
WP2 and further for other project activities
Separate work packages for activities linked to specific budget categories (D.2 Studies, D.3 Synergetic elements, D.4 Works in outermost regions, D.5 Land purchase)
For activities linked to financial support to third parties: conditions, max amounts, criteria, eligible activity types, person/category criteria, support procedures
For Works proposals: ensure consistency with detailed budget table per work package

sub.label: 6.2a Timetable
prompts: Project timetable
Interdependencies between work packages
Critical path identification

sub.label: 7.1 Ethics
prompts: Any ethical considerations relevant to the project

sub.label: 7.2 Security
prompts: Any security considerations relevant to the project

sub.label: 8.1 Declarations
prompts: Declarations as required by grant agreement
